Photograph: Shannon Stapleton/Reuters US immigration Haitians face arrest and deportation after US removes TPS protections DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin says ‘We’re going after them right now’ despite threat of violence in home country Alexandra Villarreal in New York Fri 7 Aug 2026 07.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 07.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Hundreds of thousands of Haitians are faced with the prospect of imminent risk of arrest and deportation – to a home country racked with crime, violence and political unrest – after the Trump administration officially stripped them of humanitarian protections that had allowed them to live and work legally in the United States for years. US district judge Ana Reyes confirmed on Wednesday that her order blocking the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) from ending temporary protected status (TPS) for Haiti was no longer in effect. This followed the controversial supreme court ruling in June that upended judicial review of the program and opened the door for immigration enforcement to track down and detain Haitians en masse. Supreme court conservatives accused of advancing ‘white-supremacist agenda’ Read more “We’re going after them right now,” the DHS secretary, Markwayne Mullin, said earlier this week. “These individuals can either self-deport or we’ll arrest you and send you back. It’s that simple.” Enacted by Congress in 1990, TPS protects people who are already in the US when a natural disaster, epidemic, armed conflict or other extraordinary and temporary circumstance affects their country of origin, making it unsafe for them to return home. ‘Devastating’: lives of nurses and patients upended by Trump migrant crackdown Read more TPS holders are eligible for work permits and have added an estimated $262bn to the US economy since 2001, according to the FWD.us advocacy organization, often pursuing careers in essential industries such as construction and health and elder care . But since returning to office last year, the Trump administration has almost categorically terminated existing TPS designations for some of the most dangerous countries in the world – a policy change that eventually led the highest court to authorize ending the program for Haiti and Syria , despite both countries being on the state department’s “ do not travel ” advisory list. “In a stunning contradiction, the administration advises Americans against all travel to Haiti – and instructs those who go anyway to draft a will and submit DNA samples so their remains can be identified,” said Krish O’Mara Vignarajah, president and CEO of the immigrant-serving non-profit Global Refuge. He continued: “That is the government’s own assessment of the danger. To then compel hundreds of thousands of Haitians into such dire circumstances is an unconscionable abdication of our moral responsibility.” More than 300,000 Haitians have lost TPS permission overnight and could endure deportation if they have not applied for another form of immigration relief, such as asylum in the US or a green card. For a wide swathe of people, no such pathway to citizenship exists, even if they have lived in the US for decades. Even so, the thought of returning to Haiti’s life-threatening conditions is “unimaginable” for many Haitians in the US, PBS News reported. “It’s not that we don’t want to go back to Haiti,” said Harriett Cecilia Joseph, a former TPS holder. “It’s just the situation [there] doesn’t allow us to.” Already, removal orders for Haitians in the immigration courts have soared by 96% between March and June, according to the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse (Trac). And immigration officials have started outfitting Haitians with ankle monitors to track their movements, making them easy to find and detain. “They now face an impossible choice: remain without status and risk arrest and deportation, or return to a Haiti marred by gang violence, kidnapping and the collapse of basic services,” said Vignarajah. Thousands of Syrians , although a much smaller group in the US than Haitians, may be at similar risk of repatriation after losing TPS and their affiliated work permits. At the same time, a US district court on Wednesday also allowed the federal government to end employment authorization for active TPS holders from El Salvador, Ukraine and Sudan, jeopardizing their livelihoods despite their ongoing protections against deportation. With so many immigrants suddenly barred from the workforce, business owners are being forced to let go of employees in industries already hampered by significant labor shortages. Meanwhile, Haitians and their champions are calling on the US Senate to extend TPS legislatively, through a proposal that already passed the House of Representatives in April. “We work hard, we pay our taxes, we give back to our communities and we are a big part of the engine that keeps the United States workforce in many essential industries moving,” Josiane Valsaint, a Haitian who had TPS, wrote for the Guardian. “We deserve to stay here, with our families and loved ones.” Explore more on these topics US immigration Trump administration US foreign policy Haiti US politics Caribbean Americas news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

Beállítom Baka András köztársasági elnök képviselte Magyarországot V. Harald norvég király temetésén szerdán Oslóban, közölte a Sándor-palota az MTI-vel. Harald király augusztus 28-án, pénteken reggel 6 óra 35 perckor halt meg az oslói Rikshospitalet Egyetemi Kórházban, 89 éves volt. Ő volt Európa legidősebb uralkodója, 1991 óta volt Norvégia ceremoniális államfője. A regnáló uralkodó halála esetén Norvégiában egyértelműen meghatározott a trónöröklés rendje. Utódja, az 53 éves Haakon azonnal elfoglalja majd a trónt. Harald 1937-ben született Oslo mellett, ezzel 1380 óta ő volt az első norvég uralkodó, aki Norvégiában látta meg a napvilágot. A II. világháború elől a királyi család Svédországba menekült, Harald és szülei aztán az Egyesült Államokban vészelték át a háborút. Állami gimnáziumba majd katonai iskolába járt, 1960-tól pedig Oxfordban tanult közgazdaságtant és történelmet. Ekkor már ő volt a koronaherceg, apját, V. Olafot ugyanis 1957-ben koronázták királlyá. Harald nemcsak trónörökös volt, de nagyon sikeres vitorlázó is, 1964 és 1970 között három olimpián is indult, a legjobb eredménye a 8. hely volt '64-ben. A vitorlázásban, ahogy a trónon is apját követte, aki 1928-ban olimpiai bajnok is lett. 1991-ben, V. Olaf halála után lépett trónra. Feleségével, Szonjával 1968-ban kötött házasságot. V. Harald Magyarországra először 2002-ben látogatott el feleségével, Szonja királynéval. A látogatás alkalmával Mádl Ferenc köztársasági elnök az államfőknek adományozható legmagasabb magyar állami kitüntetést, a Magyar Érdemrend nagykeresztje a lánccal elismerést adományozta a részére. Négy évvel később, 2006. október 23-án pedig részt vett az 1956-os forradalom 50. évfordulója alkalmával rendezett állami ünnepségeken is. Photograph: Courtesy Robert Hickman Missouri Husband and wife charged in shooting death of teen driving to St Louis Halloween party Alyssa Wilson, 17, was driving to a party at city zoo when prosecutors say Willie Herndon fired a gun at her car Marina Dunbar Wed 21 Oct 2026 12.07 EDT Last modified on Wed 21 Oct 2026 12.23 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Texas husband and wife are facing criminal charges following the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old girl who was driving to a Halloween celebration at the St Louis zoo when gunfire struck her vehicle on a Missouri highway. St Louis county prosecutor Melissa Price Smith announced on Monday that Willie Herndon, 43, has been charged with first-degree murder and armed criminal action in connection with the death of Alyssa Wilson. His wife, 45-year-old Taiya Herndon, is also facing a charge of hindering prosecution. The charges follow an investigation into the deadly 14 October shooting along Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri , a community north-west of St Louis. Mississippi attorney general rules fatal police shooting of one-year-old as ‘justified’ Read more Wilson was traveling southbound at about 7pm, heading to meet a friend for the zoo’s Halloween festivities, known as Boo at the Zoo, when the shooting occurred. Court documents reveal that at least one bullet was fired into the back of the teenager’s vehicle. The gunfire left Wilson “incapacitated,” according to court records, and her vehicle subsequently slammed into a concrete median barrier. Emergency responders transported the teenager to the Barnes-Jewish hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators say security footage captured crucial details that helped authorities identify the suspects. Jack Abell, chief deputy commander of the region’s major case squad, said during a news conference that Wilson had just driven past a white Buick Enclave parked along the highway shoulder when a single gunshot could be heard. “A person exited the vehicle and stood outside for a short period of time,” he said. “There was a gunshot, got back in the vehicle. The vehicle turned its hazards off and continued on.” Authorities used surveillance footage and automated license plate readers to trace the Buick, which carried an out-of-state registration, which ultimately led authorities to the Texas couple. During Monday’s press conference, Wilson’s father, Robert Hickman, spoke about the devastating loss of his daughter and the future she will never get to experience. “Alyssa was 17, excited about her life, excited about her future,” he said. “She had 60 days until she turned 18, and we were getting ready to take our first family vacation together to go to Disney for her to see her favorite person in the world, Princess Tiana, and unfortunately, she’s not going to get to do that any more. This was a senseless act.” Investigators did not disclose what may have prompted the deadly encounter. Abell confirmed that Wilson had no relationship with either of the accused individuals. Willie Herndon now faces first-degree murder and armed criminal action charges, while Taiya Herndon has been charged with hindering prosecution in connection with the teenager’s death.
